text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The European Commission agreed to start negotiations with Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovenia and Estonia about admission to the EU. The final decision will be taken next week.
- The prosecutor's office started to investigate alleged violations of anti-corruption law by 48 MPs. The inquiry will be finished on August 25.
- Parliamentary faction Fatherland and Freedom/LNNK decided to nominate Victors Jaksons, former director of the welfare ministry Medical department, to the post of state minister of health care.
- Acting general prosecutor Egils Ziedins said members of parliament cannot be government representatives in state-run companies.
- Riga's Sixth hospital has been closed.
- State energy supplier Latvenergo partly disconnected electricity from Riga maternity hospital due to unpaid debts.
- A state audit revealed that the administration of Riga Technical University has been illegally operating with students' study fees and referred the case to the prosecutor's office.

- The state statistics committee reports that foreign investors have invested 396.2 million lats from 1990 to the end of 1996. The Latvian Development Agency forecasts that Latvia may receive $150-170 million investment in the near future.

- Deputy chairman of Riga city council Andris Argalis signed a contract with Skanska International Building on building an office bloc in the centre of Riga, in which Skanska plans to invest about $20 million.
